title: Cross-Border Traffic Fairer with SLO-Backed Credits
creator: Lina Gomez
description:
Problem statement: Our current geo-routing favors lowest-latency regions aggressively which can starve small regions and cause cascading capacity failures during spikes. We need a new cross-border traffic allocator that: 1) enforces SLO-respecting latency-aware routing, 2) preserves regional locality (geo pinning) for sticky customers where possible, and 3) gracefully sheds load when global capacity is constrained using per-region SLO-backed credit accounts.

Goal: Implement the Cross-Border Traffic Fairer (CBTF) — an orchestration component that computes per-request routing scores using latency quantiles, region-locality weight, and a region credit balance derived from SLO burn rate. The CBTF will be integrated into the request director ahead of the existing dispatch layer and must provide transparent metrics for tracing decisions and allow gradual rollout and rollback by weight percent.

Scope: This ticket covers design, simulation, circuit-breaker integration, metrics, and an initial canary implementation behind the director flag. It does NOT include long-term autoscaling policy changes or billing adjustments. Those will be follow-ups.

Non-goals: Changing the kernel scheduler, modifying model selection logic, or altering dedicated capacity quotas in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by SRE and Product: outlines algorithm, thresholds, and fallback behaviors
Simulations show no more than 5% increase in 99th p50 latency for pinned requests under synthetic spikes while reducing cross-region evictions by 20%
Canary deployed to 1% traffic with director flag, with live metrics showing per-region credit accounting and decision traces

Circuit breaker integration: each region exposes a CBTF-compatible token that can be consumed and replenished; requests are shed with clear error class (HTTP 429 with X-Redwood-Fairer) when credits exhausted
Runbook appended: steps to escalate, rollback, or adjust credit refill rates; playbook for tenant-impacting events
design_notes:
High-level algorithm: 1) Compute latency_score = normalized(latency_quantile / target_quantile) where quantile is 95th tail measured over sliding window. 2) locality_score = pinned ? 0.9 : 0.5 (configurable per-customer) to bias toward keeping requests local. 3) credit_factor = sigmoid(available_credits / credit_capacity) so that regions with depleted credits are deprioritized. 4) final_score = w1*(1/latency_score) + w2*locality_score + w3*credit_factor - penalty_for_recent_errors. 5) Soft-hedge: if top candidate's score is within epsilon of second-best, prefer local for pinned customers unless credits exhausted.

Credit model: Each region maintains a sliding credit bucket replenished at rate proportional to region capacity and SLO headroom. Credits are consumed based on cost_units for routed requests (token count * cost_weight) and also on excess latency incidents to account for noisier hardware. Refill curve is tunable; default: linear refill with small burst buffer. Credits are persisted in regional control plane and replicated to read-only caches to avoid single-point-of-failure.

Circuit breaker integration: Hook into existing region circuit breaker API. When region breaker trips, CBTF sets credit to zero and routes proactively away except for P0 pinned requests when explicit override flag is provided by SEs. Breaker state changes are treated as high-priority telemetry events and emitted to the director trace stream.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: Lab simulation and small-scale inject testing (2 days). Phase 2: Canary to 1% of traffic (72 hours) with live dashboards and automated anomaly detection on latency and error rates. Phase 3: Ramp by 5x every 24 hours pending no sustained regressions; stop conditions include >3% increase in p95 for any region or >2x increase in 5xx rate. Phase 4: 100% rollout and tuning. Each ramp step must include a postmortem template if stop conditions met. Default rollback is to previous director behavior.

Safety knobs available: runtime flag to disable CBTF, per-tenant locality_override flag, global credit refill multiplier, and immediate drain to zero (fast-shed) for emergency stabilization.
observability_and_alerting: Telemetry: per-region credit_balance (gauge), credit_consumed/sec, routed_requests_by_candidate (histogram), decision_traces (sampled distributed traces), circuit_breaker_state (enum), shed_reasons (counter). Dashboards: region fairness heatmap (requests routed vs pinned demand), leaderboard of regions by credit utilization, and drift alerts for pinned customer SLO violations. Alerts: page on sustained depletion of credits in >2 consecutive regions, alert on sudden >10% increase in shed rate within 5m, and alert on canary regression thresholds described in rollout_plan.
testing_strategy: Unit tests for scoring math and edge conditions. End-to-end simulator that replays historical traffic traces with synthetic spikes to validate fairness and stability. Chaos tests: simulate partial control plane partitions where credit reads are stale and verify conservative fallback (treat unknown as low credit). Integration tests to verify header X-Redwood-Fairer appears on shed responses and that director respects override header for pinned P0 requests.

comments: 2026-03-01 Marcus Holt: Initial design posted. Need feedback from telemetry on metric granularity (histogram vs summary) — preferring histogram for flexible quantiles.

2026-03-02 Emily Chen (SRE): Suggest adding conservative mode when control plane partition occurs. If credit status unknown, default to 'low' instead of allowing routing that may oversubscribe remote region.
2026-03-03 Rajesh Kapoor (Product): Request a privacy note re: per-tenant locality flags and visibility into customer pinning; compliance wants assurance we don't leak tenant affinity across teams.
2026-03-04 Lina Gomez: Added canary stop conditions and fleshed out shed HTTP response (429 + X-Redwood-Fairer + JSON reason). Created stub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/director/pull/4090

2026-03-05 Marcus Holt: Ran simulation with last quarter traffic. Results: average routed cross-region traffic reduced by 18% under spike, pinned p95 increased by 1.8% (within target). Found edge-case where very low-volume region starved credits due to high replenishment granularity; created follow-up ENG-504011 to add fractional refill smoothing.
notes_for_followups: 1) Autoscaler integration: use credit trends as a hint to spin temporary capacity in heavily-shedding regions. 2) Billing: evaluate whether cross-region routing should incur cross-region cost multiplier. 3) UX: expose per-tenant locality preference in Console and allow legal approvals for overriding default locality. Create tickets for each after full canary.
